correctness.rationale: The exact finite search has a proved bijection to order-five de Bruijn necklaces: Eulerian tours in the 16-vertex, 32-edge directed de Bruijn graph, canonically rooted at the unique 00000 edge. Independently all \(2^{16}\) incoming/outgoing local bijections give the same 2048 canonical cycles. The suffix-palindrome dynamic-programming recurrence exactly minimizes nonempty factor count, and a distinct center-expansion implementation agrees on all 65,536 rooted words. The saved standalone verifier exhaustively checks the two complete tables, totals and exceptional cases. Finite exhaustive proof is appropriate here since the claim is finite, not infinite.

value.rationale: Shortest palindrome partitions are a natural nonlocal factorization invariant. De Bruijn sequences fix every five-bit factor exactly once, making their distinct cut-dependent palindrome partition lengths a direct measure of global arrangement rather than factor vocabulary. Order five is a motivated complete finite cutoff (2048 cycles, compared with 67,108,864 at order six). The result determines all possible lengths with exact multiplicities, every cycle best/worst-cut pair, strict rotation sensitivity for every cycle, and a uniquely small two-cycle hardest-best-cut class. These do not follow from the generalized K(32) bound or individual palindrome factor lengths. It claims no unwarranted all-order theorem.
